div.head: Hl 5[b]
div.ab: gif he þæt ne mæge, gelde swa he gono háge.
gif he þæt ne mæge, gelde swa he genoh áge.
Gif he þæt ne mæge, gelde swa he gonoh áge.
wenn er das [Eidleisten] nicht kann, so zahle er [dem Kläger und dem Richter] sofern er [dazu] genug besitzt.
if he cannot do that [take the oath], then let him pay [the plaintiff and the judge] so far as he possesses enough [for it].
If he cannot do this, he must pay to the best of his ability.
If he is not able to do that [oath-swearing], let him pay to the extent he owns enough.

note.seg: Zeilenende, aber dahinter Bindestrich, welcher vielleicht gonoh áge zu lesen bedeutet
End of line, but followed by a hyphen, which perhaps indicates that gonoh áge is to be read

‘wenn’ s. Wb swa III D; falsch Frühere ‘soviel wie ausreicht’. Price vergleicht Lex Baiuwar. I. II, 1: usque habet substantiam, componat; si vero non habet, ipse se in servitio deprimat; vgl. Gl Verknechtung. Bevor diese eintrat, hielt sich wohl Kläger und Richter an den subsidiär Haftbaren (ECf 23, 3), hier wohl die Sippe des Missetäters. Der Betrag der Buss- und Strafsumme fehlt, wohl nicht durch Lücke der Hs. Entweder stand er fest wie bei anderen Germanen, die halbes oder volles oder mehrfaches Wergeld dafür fordern (Wilda 797f.; Richthofen in Mon. Germ., Leg. V 59) oder wechselte vielleicht nach Stand des Geraubten [Dass der Menschendieb emendet ei (dem Verkauften) iuxta quod placitare potuit (Lex Sax. 20), gehört nicht hierher, da jener ihn zurückgebracht hat]

‘if’: see Wb swa III D; earlier translators wrongly have ‘as much as suffices’. Price compares Lex Baiuwar. I. II, 1: usque habet substantiam, componat; si vero non habet, ipse se in servitio deprimat; cf. Gl Verknechtung. Before this took effect, plaintiff and judge probably had recourse to the party subsidiarily liable (ECf 23, 3), here probably the offender’s kindred. The amount of the compensation and fine is not given, probably not because of a lacuna in the MS. Either it was fixed, as among other Germanic peoples, who demand half, full or multiple wergild for it (Wilda 797f.; Richthofen in Mon. Germ., Leg. V 59), or it perhaps varied with the rank of the person carried off [That the man-stealer emendet ei (the person sold) iuxta quod placitare potuit (Lex Sax. 20) is not relevant here, since there he has brought him back]
geonhagie zu emendieren ist unnütz. h unorganisch vor anlautendem Vokal: s. Wb 107 Sp. 2 — gonoh für genoh ist möglich; ebd. 159 Sp. 2
There is no point in emending to geonhagie. h is inorganic before an initial vowel: see Wb 107 col. 2 — gonoh for genoh is possible; ibid. 159 col. 2

note.label: Gif
note.seg: g is lower case; there is no point after preceding tohyre.

note.label: áge.
note.seg: The line break occurs after gono, but this is almost surely to be divided gonoh age; Whitelock, English Historical Documents, 394, points out that the copyist ‘may have been influenced by the verb onhagian which can mean “to afford.”’
